# Ordered fragment manifest for codebase-audit/workflow.js (#806).
#
# EDIT THE FRAGMENTS, NOT THE ARTIFACT. ../workflow.js is generated by
# concatenating the files below IN THIS ORDER — an edit made directly to it is
# overwritten by the next `just gen-workflow-js`, and until then
# tests/lint-workflow-js-generated.sh fails the tree as stale.
#
# THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, WHICH IS WHY THIS LIST IS EXPLICIT AND NOT A GLOB:
#
#   00-meta.js MUST stay first. The engine rejects a script whose
#   `export const meta` is not the very first statement.
#
#   40-injection-utils.js MUST precede 50-output-paths.js. `auditDir` is
#   initialized at MODULE LOAD by calling `sanitizeDir`, so reversing the two is
#   a temporal-dead-zone throw. The fragment boundaries here follow the file's
#   own section banners, which already encode this: the "Audit output paths"
#   banner reads "(need sanitizeDir above)".
#
# The generator checks this list against the directory in BOTH directions: a
# listed fragment missing on disk fails, and an unlisted `.js` sitting in this
# directory fails too — the second is the dangerous one, since it is a file
# someone edits believing it ships while the artifact holds none of its bytes.
# Same contract, same reasoning, as tests/lib/fragments.sh.

00-meta.js               # export const meta — must be the FIRST statement
10-config.js             # scope/depth/output/timestamp input parsing
20-budget-guards.js      # BUDGET_FLOOR, TAIL_FLOOR, tailAgent, attempt, template
30-schemas.js            # CERTAINTY / FINDING / MAP / SCAN / VERIFY / AGGREGATE …
40-injection-utils.js    # READONLY, sanitize, slugify, sanitizeDir — before 50
50-output-paths.js       # auditDir, outDir, reportPath (call sanitizeDir)
60-prompts.js            # stableStringify, dataBlock, prompt builders
70-result-plumbing.js    # stampRefs, applyVerifyScores, finalResult
80-orchestration.js      # the side-effecting body (past ORCH_BOUNDARY)
